# Integration-test targets that legitimately execute ZERO tests under the default
# `cargo test --tests` command, because their contents are behind a non-default
# cargo feature (`code-graph`, `mcp-endpoint`, `graph-rag`, `internal-tests`).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `docs/GATES.md` §3b makes "a suite reporting
# `ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored` ran nothing" a gate FAILURE. That rule is right for a
# suite that is SUPPOSED to run — it is how a silently-emptied suite gets caught — but the
# targets below are opt-ins that are empty BY DESIGN without their feature. The first
# `integration full` run failed all six shards on exactly these, so the check now consults
# this allowlist and fails only on a suite that is not listed.
#
# Generated from a full local run:
#   awk '/^     Running/{s=$2} /^test result: ok\. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored/{print s}' full.log
#
# MAINTENANCE. Removing a name makes the gate strict for that suite again. Adding one
# suppresses a real signal — only do so with the feature gate that justifies it. Note the
# `internal-tests` entries (branch_*, time_travel_*, encryption_tests, materialized_view_tests,
# protocol_integration_test, repl_tenant_commands, …) DO run in the `feature-gated-compile`
# tier and in the local `--features internal-tests` gate; they are empty only by default.
